blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, was afraid of the Hebrew people because they were growing so many. So he gave a cruel order. Every Hebrew baby boy was to be thrown into the river. The girls could live.

verses.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

segments.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

verses.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A goodly child. His mother looked at her baby boy and could not give him up. For three months she hid him. Imagine the fear of keeping a newborn quiet, every cry a danger.

verses.text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

segments.text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When she could hide him no longer, she made a little ark out of bulrushes. She sealed it with slime and pitch so it would float. She laid her baby inside and set it among the reeds at the edge of the river. The same river Pharaoh meant for death, she trusted to carry life.

verses.text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: His big sister stood watching from a distance. She did not leave him. She wanted to know what would happen to her brother.

verses.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

verses.text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

segments.text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said,

segments.speaker: daughter
segments.text: This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The baby was crying, and the daughter of Pharaoh had compassion on him. She knew he was a Hebrew child, one of the very babies her father had ordered killed. She chose mercy anyway.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then the sister stepped forward. Think how brave that was, a young Hebrew girl speaking up to the daughter of Pharaoh.

verses.text: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

segments.speaker: sister
segments.text: Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

verses.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.

segments.text: And the maid went and called the child’s mother.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The sister ran and brought her own mother, the baby's mother.

verses.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The mother who had hidden her son and placed him in the river was now handed him back. She would nurse him, and she would be paid for it. Her son was safe in her arms again.

verses.text: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The boy grew. When he was older, his mother brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, because she drew him out of the water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This story turns on a few women. A mother who would not give up her son. A sister who watched and spoke up. A princess who chose compassion over her father's order. Through them, God preserved the child who would one day lead his people out of Egypt.
